courses.title: Basics
courses.line: The board, the moves, check and checkmate.

lessons.title: The board and the pieces
lessons.line: Where each piece starts, a light square in the right corner, the queen on her own color.

lessons.title: Naming the squares
lessons.line: Files a to h, ranks 1 to 8: every square has a name, from a1 to h8.

lessons.title: Reading moves
lessons.line: How a move is written: e4, Nf3, Bxc6, O-O, and what + and # mean.

lessons.title: How the pieces move: an overview
lessons.line: All six pieces, one board each. The lessons after it take each piece up close.

lessons.title: The rook and the bishop
lessons.line: Straight lines and diagonals, and what stops them.

lessons.title: The queen
lessons.line: A rook and a bishop in one piece.

lessons.title: The knight
lessons.line: The only piece that jumps. Reach any square in the fewest moves.

lessons.title: The king
lessons.line: One square at a time, and never onto an attacked square.

lessons.title: The pawn
lessons.line: Forward one, two on its first move, and it captures diagonally.

lessons.title: Promotion and en passant
lessons.line: A pawn on the last rank becomes a queen or another piece; the one capture that lands behind a pawn.

lessons.title: Castling
lessons.line: King and rook in one move, on either side.

lessons.title: When you cannot castle
lessons.line: After the king or that rook has moved, out of check, through check or into check.

lessons.title: What the pieces are worth
lessons.line: Pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, and why the king has no number.

lessons.title: Good and bad trades
lessons.line: When giving a piece for a piece leaves you ahead.

lessons.title: Attackers and defenders
lessons.line: Count them before you capture.

lessons.title: Check
lessons.line: The king is attacked. Three ways out: move it, block, or capture the attacker.

lessons.title: Checkmate and stalemate
lessons.line: Check with no way out wins. No legal move and no check is a draw.

lessons.title: Draws and resigning
lessons.line: Repetition, too little to mate, the fifty-move rule, agreement, and giving up a lost game.

lessons.title: Before every move
lessons.line: Ask what the other side's last move attacks, then answer it: move, guard or capture.

courses.title: Openings
courses.line: Openings to choose as White, and defenses to choose as Black.

lessons.title: Three rules for the opening
lessons.line: Take the center, bring out the knights and bishops, castle.

lessons.title: Moving a piece twice
lessons.line: Each move in the opening should bring out a piece that has not moved yet, unless moving again gains something.

lessons.title: The queen out early
lessons.line: An early queen can make threats, but every attack on her brings out one of your pieces.

lessons.title: Gambits
lessons.line: A pawn given up early can buy time, open lines and the center.

lessons.title: Transpositions
lessons.line: The same position can come from different move orders.

lessons.title: Learning a line
lessons.line: Know why each move is played. Moves learned by heart fall apart when the other side plays something else.

chapters.title: Italian Game
chapters.line: The bishop takes aim at Black's weakest square, and White gets ready to open the center.

lessons.title: Italian Game: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop aims at Black's weakest square, and White gets ready to open the center.

lessons.title: Italian Game: Center Attack
lessons.line: White opens the center at once with two pawns side by side.

lessons.title: Italian Game: Giuoco Pianissimo
lessons.line: White keeps the center closed and builds up slowly, the way most strong players do today.

lessons.title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit
lessons.line: White gives a pawn to win time and build the center.

lessons.title: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense
lessons.line: Black attacks White's center pawn instead of copying the bishop, and gives a pawn for quick play.

lessons.title: Italian Game: Fried Liver Attack
lessons.line: When Black takes back with the knight, White gives a knight on f7 and drags the king out.

lessons.title: Italian Game: the Blackburne Shilling trap
lessons.line: A pawn left out as bait: taking it walks into mate.

chapters.title: Ruy Lopez
chapters.line: The bishop presses on the knight that guards Black's center pawn, for a long, slow fight.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop presses on the knight that guards Black's center pawn.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Closed
lessons.line: The main line: White builds a big center slowly, and both sides maneuver.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White gives the bishop for the knight to spoil Black's pawns, and aims for an endgame.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense
lessons.line: Black attacks the center pawn at once, and the queens often come off early.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Open
lessons.line: Black takes the center pawn and plays actively; White opens lines and wins the pawn back.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Attack
lessons.line: Black gives a pawn to send its pieces at the white king.

lessons.title: Ruy Lopez: Noah's Ark trap
lessons.line: Black's pawns chase the queen and then trap White's bishop.

chapters.title: Scotch Game
chapters.line: White opens the center at once and gets free play for its pieces.

lessons.title: Scotch Game: the ideas
lessons.line: White opens the center at once and gets free play for its pieces.

lessons.title: Scotch Game: Classical Variation
lessons.line: Black's bishop hits the knight in the center and aims at the pawn beside White's king.

lessons.title: Scotch Game: Mieses Variation
lessons.line: Black's knight attacks the center pawn; White trades knights and pushes the pawn to chase it.

lessons.title: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit
lessons.line: White brings the bishop out before taking the pawn back, and offers more if Black is greedy.

chapters.title: Four Knights Game
chapters.line: Both sides bring out both knights first, for a calm and sound game.

lessons.title: Four Knights Game: the ideas
lessons.line: Both sides bring out both knights first: a calm, sound start.

lessons.title: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation
lessons.line: The bishop pins the knight as in the Ruy Lopez, and Black answers by jumping into the center.

lessons.title: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation
lessons.line: White opens the center with all four knights already out.

lessons.title: Four Knights Game: meeting the Halloween Gambit
lessons.line: Seen from Black's side: White gives a knight for a pawn and chases the black knights.

chapters.title: Petrov's Defense
chapters.line: Black does not guard its center pawn: it attacks White's instead.

lessons.title: Petrov's Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black does not guard its center pawn: it attacks White's instead.

lessons.title: Petrov's Defense: Three Knights Game
lessons.line: White guards the center pawn with a knight. Black pins that knight and wins the pawn back.

lessons.title: Petrov's Defense: Modern Attack
lessons.line: White pushes into the center at once. Black takes the pawn on e4 and trades off the strong white knight.

lessons.title: Petrov's Defense: the Damiano trap
lessons.line: Taking back the pawn on e4 too soon lets the white queen come out, and one more slip loses yours.

chapters.title: Philidor Defense
chapters.line: A pawn guards the center pawn: a solid start that gives the pieces less room.

lessons.title: Philidor Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: A pawn guards the center pawn: solid, with less room for the pieces.

lessons.title: Philidor Defense: Hanham Variation
lessons.line: Black keeps its pawn on e5 with a knight behind it, and must watch the weak pawn by its king.

lessons.title: Philidor Defense: Légal's mate
lessons.line: White gives up the queen and mates with three minor pieces, if Black takes it.

chapters.title: King's Gambit
chapters.line: White gives a pawn to build the center and open a file for the rook.

lessons.title: King's Gambit: the ideas
lessons.line: White gives a pawn to build the center and open a file for the rook.

lessons.title: King's Gambit Accepted
lessons.line: Black takes the pawn and guards it with more pawns. White breaks them up.

lessons.title: King's Gambit Declined: Classical Variation
lessons.line: Black does not take: its bishop stops White's king from castling on the short side.

lessons.title: King's Gambit: Falkbeer Countergambit
lessons.line: Black answers the gambit with a pawn offer of its own in the center.

chapters.title: Vienna Game
chapters.line: The knight comes out first, and the pawn on f2 is ready to push.

lessons.title: Vienna Game: the ideas
lessons.line: The knight comes out first, and the pawn on f2 is ready to push.

lessons.title: Vienna Game: Vienna Gambit
lessons.line: The King's Gambit idea with a knight already out. Black strikes back in the center.

lessons.title: Vienna Game: Max Lange Defense
lessons.line: Black brings the other knight out first. White aims at f7 and keeps the pawn on f2 ready.

chapters.title: Bishop's Opening
chapters.line: The bishop comes out first, and White keeps its choices open.

lessons.title: Bishop's Opening: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop comes out first, and White keeps its choices open.

chapters.title: Sicilian Defense
chapters.line: Black fights for the center from the side, for a sharp, unbalanced game.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black fights for the center from the side, for an unbalanced game.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation
lessons.line: A quiet pawn move keeps White's pieces out, then a center pawn kicks the knight away.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation
lessons.line: The bishop goes to the long diagonal and aims at the side where White's king often castles.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Classical Variation
lessons.line: Both knights come out first, and the queen can join them against White's knight in the center.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Scheveningen Variation
lessons.line: Two pawns make a small, solid center, and a strike in the middle answers White's attack on the wing.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Sveshnikov Variation
lessons.line: Black leaves a hole in the center to chase White's knights and get active pieces.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Taimanov and Kan
lessons.line: A pawn one step forward keeps Black flexible, and the queen watches the open file.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Accelerated Dragon
lessons.line: The bishop comes out early, and the queen's pawn waits to go two squares in one move.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Alapin Variation
lessons.line: White gets ready for a second center pawn; Black hits back at once, and the queen can come out early.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Closed Variation
lessons.line: White keeps the center closed and builds up on the king's side; Black's pieces take the long diagonal and the center.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Grand Prix Attack
lessons.line: White pushes a pawn on the king's side and aims a bishop at Black's king; Black blocks it and strikes in the center.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Smith-Morra Gambit
lessons.line: White gives a pawn for fast development; Black takes it, and a careless move by White meets a trap.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Rossolimo Attack
lessons.line: White's bishop pins the knight and may trade itself for it; Black gets two bishops and open lines.

lessons.title: Sicilian Defense: Moscow Variation
lessons.line: White checks with a bishop to trade it off; Black blocks with its own bishop and builds a center.

chapters.title: French Defense
chapters.line: Black builds a solid pawn chain, then strikes at the base of White's center.

lessons.title: French Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black builds a solid pawn chain, then strikes at the base of White's center.

lessons.title: French Defense: Advance Variation
lessons.line: White takes space with a pawn chain; Black piles up on its base and steps around a well-known trap.

lessons.title: French Defense: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White trades in the center, the position opens, and Black's shut-in bishop is free.

lessons.title: French Defense: Tarrasch Variation
lessons.line: White's knight guards the center from behind; Black hits White's pawn chain twice.

lessons.title: French Defense: Winawer Variation
lessons.line: The bishop pins the knight, and Black gives it up to double White's pawns.

lessons.title: French Defense: Classical Variation
lessons.line: A knight hits the center, the bishop breaks the pin, and a pawn strikes the chain.

lessons.title: French Defense: Rubinstein Variation
lessons.line: Black gives up the center pawn for easy development and trades White's strong knight.

chapters.title: Caro-Kann Defense
chapters.line: Like the French, but a side pawn backs up the center and leaves a bishop free to come out.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Like the French, but the side pawn leaves a bishop free to come out before the pawns close it in.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical Variation
lessons.line: The bishop comes out with a hit on the knight, and Black keeps it safe from White's h-pawn.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Advance Variation
lessons.line: White's pawn pushes past; Black's bishop comes out first, then a pawn hits the base of the chain.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Karpov Variation
lessons.line: A knight comes out first to back up the other one, and Black steps around a famous mate.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White trades in the center for a quiet game; Black's bishop gets out before the pawns close it in.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Panov Attack
lessons.line: White plays for active pieces with a lone pawn in the center; Black sits a knight in front of it.

lessons.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Two Knights Attack
lessons.line: White brings both knights out first; Black gives a bishop for a knight and builds the center.

chapters.title: Scandinavian Defense
chapters.line: Black hits White's center pawn on the first move and takes it back at once.

lessons.title: Scandinavian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black hits White's center pawn at once, takes back with the queen, then finds her a safe square.

lessons.title: Scandinavian Defense: Gubinsky-Melts Defense
lessons.line: The queen steps back to the center, and a side pawn keeps White's knight away from her.

lessons.title: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation
lessons.line: Black takes the pawn back later with a knight, and the knight settles in front of White's pawns.

chapters.title: Pirc Defense
chapters.line: Black lets White build a center, aims a bishop at it from the side, and attacks it later.

lessons.title: Pirc Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black lets White build a center, puts a bishop on the long diagonal, and strikes at the center later.

lessons.title: Pirc Defense: Austrian Attack
lessons.line: White builds a wall of three center pawns; Black castles and hits the wall from the side.

lessons.title: Pirc Defense: 150 Attack
lessons.line: White brings the bishop and the queen out together to attack; Black takes space on the queen's side and hits the center.

chapters.title: Modern Defense
chapters.line: The bishop goes to the long diagonal before anything else, and Black stays flexible.

lessons.title: Modern Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop goes to the long diagonal at once, and Black keeps the knights home to stay flexible.

chapters.title: Alekhine Defense
chapters.line: The knight invites White's pawns forward so that Black can attack them.

lessons.title: Alekhine Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: The knight invites White's pawns forward, and Black attacks them once they are far from home.

lessons.title: Alekhine Defense: Modern Variation
lessons.line: White develops calmly; Black trades the center pawn and steps around a famous knight sacrifice.

lessons.title: Alekhine Defense: Four Pawns Attack
lessons.line: White takes all the space offered with four pawns; Black's pieces attack the big center.

lessons.title: Alekhine Defense: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White trades pawns; Black takes back toward the center and later strikes with the other center pawn.

chapters.title: Queen's Gambit
chapters.line: White offers a side pawn to pull Black's center pawn away.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit: the ideas
lessons.line: White offers a side pawn to pull Black's center pawn away.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit Accepted
lessons.line: Black takes the offered pawn, and White gets it back with easy development.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense
lessons.line: Black holds the center with pawns, and White aims a rook down the c-file.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White trades pawns in the center, then pushes two queenside pawns against three.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tartakower Defense
lessons.line: Black makes room for its shut in bishop, and White trades pieces and presses on the c-file.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Ragozin Defense
lessons.line: Black pins the knight on c3 with a bishop, and White breaks the pin.

lessons.title: Queen's Gambit: traps
lessons.line: Two traps: Black holding on to the pawn, and a pawn on d5 that is not free.

chapters.title: Slav Defense
chapters.line: A pawn on c6 holds the center, and the bishop stays free to come out.

lessons.title: Slav Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: A pawn on c6 holds the center, and the bishop stays free to come out.

lessons.title: Slav Defense: Czech Variation
lessons.line: Black takes on c4, brings the bishop out, and pins the knight on c3.

lessons.title: Slav Defense: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White trades pawns at once, and both sides have the same pawns.

chapters.title: Semi-Slav Defense
chapters.line: Two pawns hold the center, and Black waits for the moment to take on c4 or strike back.

lessons.title: Semi-Slav Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Two pawns hold the center, then Black takes on c4 and strikes back with the king pawn.

lessons.title: Semi-Slav Defense: Meran Variation
lessons.line: Black takes on c4 and pushes the queenside pawns forward, chasing the bishop.

lessons.title: Semi-Slav Defense: Botvinnik Variation
lessons.line: Black takes on c4 and keeps it, while White attacks on the kingside. Sharp for both.

chapters.title: Tarrasch Defense
chapters.line: Black takes a lone center pawn in return for open lines for its pieces.

lessons.title: Tarrasch Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black strikes at the center at once and gets open lines for every piece.

lessons.title: Tarrasch Defense: the main line
lessons.line: Black gets a lone pawn on d5, and open lines for its pieces in return.

chapters.title: Albin Countergambit
chapters.line: Black answers the gambit with one of its own, and a pawn wedged deep in White's camp.

lessons.title: Albin Countergambit: the ideas
lessons.line: Black offers a pawn of its own and wedges a pawn deep into White's camp.

lessons.title: Albin Countergambit: the Lasker Trap
lessons.line: A pawn marches to the last rank and becomes a knight, with check.

chapters.title: London System
chapters.line: The same calm setup against almost anything, with the bishop out early.

lessons.title: London System: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop comes out early, then pawns build a solid triangle behind it.

lessons.title: London System against the King's Indian setup
lessons.line: The same plan when Black puts its bishop on the long diagonal.

chapters.title: King's Indian Defense
chapters.line: Black lets White build a big center, then strikes at it.

lessons.title: King's Indian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black lets White build a big center, then strikes at it.

lessons.title: King's Indian Defense: Mar del Plata Variation
lessons.line: The center locks. White attacks on the queen's side, and Black storms the king.

lessons.title: King's Indian Defense: Sämisch Variation
lessons.line: A pawn holds White's center, and the kings often castle on opposite wings.

lessons.title: King's Indian Defense: Four Pawns Attack
lessons.line: White takes all the center it can, and Black attacks the pawns before they settle.

lessons.title: King's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation
lessons.line: White's bishop guards its king from the long diagonal, so Black plays on the queen's side.

chapters.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense
chapters.line: The bishop pins White's knight, so White's king's pawn cannot safely come to the center.

lessons.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop pins White's knight, so White's king's pawn cannot safely come to the center.

lessons.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Rubinstein System
lessons.line: White develops quietly, and Black takes a full share of the center with pawns.

lessons.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Classical Variation
lessons.line: White's queen is ready to take back if the bishop takes the knight, so White's pawns stay whole.

lessons.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Sämisch Variation
lessons.line: White takes the two bishops at the cost of doubled pawns, and Black attacks the front one.

chapters.title: Queen's Indian Defense
chapters.line: The bishop on the long diagonal and the knight hold a key center square.

lessons.title: Queen's Indian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: The bishop on the long diagonal and the knight hold a key center square.

lessons.title: Queen's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation
lessons.line: Both bishops face each other on the long diagonal, and the fight is for a center square on it.

lessons.title: Queen's Indian Defense: Petrosian Variation
lessons.line: A pawn keeps the black bishop out, and White aims to take the center with the king's pawn.

chapters.title: Bogo-Indian Defense
chapters.line: A bishop check makes White block with a piece, and Black trades it off.

lessons.title: Bogo-Indian Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: A bishop check makes White block with a piece, and Black trades it off.

chapters.title: Grünfeld Defense
chapters.line: Black lets White take the center with pawns, then attacks it with pieces.

lessons.title: Grünfeld Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: Black strikes at the center with a pawn at once, then hits White's pawns with the bishop, a side pawn and the queen.

lessons.title: Grünfeld Defense: Exchange Variation
lessons.line: White gets a big center of pawns, and Black's bishop on the long diagonal attacks it.

lessons.title: Grünfeld Defense: Russian Variation
lessons.line: White's queen comes out early and White builds the center, and Black chases the queen with pawns.

chapters.title: Benoni Defense
chapters.line: An unbalanced game: Black has more pawns on the queen's side, White more in the center.

lessons.title: Benoni Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: An unbalanced game: Black has more pawns on the queen's side, White more in the center.

lessons.title: Benoni Defense: Classical Variation
lessons.line: White develops calmly, and Black's rook and knight aim at White's center pawn.

chapters.title: Benko Gambit
chapters.line: Black gives a pawn to open two files on the queen's side for its rooks.

lessons.title: Benko Gambit: the ideas
lessons.line: Black gives a pawn to open two files on the queen's side for its rooks.

lessons.title: Benko Gambit: the main line
lessons.line: For the pawn, Black's queen, rooks and bishop all bear down on White's queen's side.

chapters.title: Budapest Gambit
chapters.line: Black gives a center pawn for quick play with the pieces, and usually wins it back.

lessons.title: Budapest Gambit: the ideas
lessons.line: Black gives a center pawn for quick play with the pieces, and usually wins it back.

chapters.title: Catalan Opening
chapters.line: The Queen's Gambit with a bishop on the long diagonal, aimed at Black's queen's side.

lessons.title: Catalan Opening: the ideas
lessons.line: The Queen's Gambit with a bishop on the long diagonal, aimed at Black's queen's side.

lessons.title: Catalan Opening: Open Defense
lessons.line: Black takes White's side pawn, and White wins it back while the bishop watches the long diagonal.

lessons.title: Catalan Opening: Closed
lessons.line: Black keeps its center pawn, and White gets the king's pawn ready to push and take more space.

chapters.title: Dutch Defense
chapters.line: From the first move, Black fights for the center with a pawn from the king's side.

lessons.title: Dutch Defense: the ideas
lessons.line: From the first move, Black fights for the center with a pawn from the king's side.

lessons.title: Dutch Defense: Leningrad Variation
lessons.line: Black puts its bishop on the long diagonal and gets ready to push the king's pawn.

lessons.title: Dutch Defense: Stonewall Variation
lessons.line: Four pawns hold the center like a wall and leave a hole in front of it that no pawn can guard.

lessons.title: Dutch Defense: Staunton Gambit
lessons.line: White gives a pawn at once to open lines against Black's king.

chapters.title: English Opening
chapters.line: The c-pawn goes first and fights for the center from the side.

lessons.title: English Opening: the ideas
lessons.line: The c-pawn goes first, a bishop watches the long diagonal, and the queenside pawns march.

lessons.title: English Opening: King's English Variation
lessons.line: A Sicilian Defense with the colors reversed, and White has an extra move.

lessons.title: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation
lessons.line: Black copies White move for move, until White breaks the symmetry in the center.

lessons.title: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defense
lessons.line: Black brings the knight out first, and White takes the whole center with pawns.

chapters.title: Réti Opening
chapters.line: The knight goes first, then a side pawn strikes at Black's center pawn.

lessons.title: Réti Opening: the ideas
lessons.line: The knight goes first, a side pawn attacks the center, and both bishops aim at it from the side.

chapters.title: King's Indian Attack
chapters.line: A calm setup with the bishop on the long diagonal, then a pawn push and an attack on the king.

lessons.title: King's Indian Attack: the ideas
lessons.line: A calm setup behind the bishop on the long diagonal, then a pawn push toward the king.

chapters.title: Bird Opening
chapters.line: The f-pawn goes first and takes hold of a center square on Black's half of the board.

lessons.title: Bird Opening: the ideas
lessons.line: The f-pawn and a bishop on the long diagonal take hold of a center square for a knight.

lessons.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit
lessons.line: Black gives a pawn to aim the queen and bishop at White's king.

courses.title: Tactics
courses.line: Forks, pins and attacks on the king.

lessons.title: Pieces left hanging
lessons.line: Before every move: checks, captures, threats, and is anything of yours or theirs undefended.

lessons.title: The fork
lessons.line: One piece attacks two at once. The knight does it best.

lessons.title: Queen and pawn forks
lessons.line: The queen attacks in eight directions; the pawn, the smallest piece, attacks two bigger ones.

lessons.title: The pin
lessons.line: A piece cannot move without exposing a bigger one behind it.

lessons.title: Breaking a pin
lessons.line: Block, move the piece behind, or attack the pinning piece.

lessons.title: The skewer
lessons.line: A pin turned around: the bigger piece in front must move and the one behind falls.

lessons.title: X-ray
lessons.line: A piece working through another piece on the same line.

lessons.title: Discovered attack
lessons.line: Move one piece and uncover an attack by another.

lessons.title: Discovered and double check
lessons.line: The uncovered piece gives check, so the moving piece can take anything; when both give check, only a king move answers it.

lessons.title: The windmill
lessons.line: Discovered checks one after another, taking a piece each time.

lessons.title: Removing the defender
lessons.line: Capture or chase the piece that holds everything together.

lessons.title: Deflection and overloading
lessons.line: Pull a defender away from the square it guards, often one defender with two jobs.

lessons.title: Decoy
lessons.line: Give something up to lure a piece onto a square where it can be hit.

lessons.title: Interference
lessons.line: Put a piece between a defender and what it defends.

lessons.title: Clearance
lessons.line: Move a piece out of the way of another.

lessons.title: Trapped pieces
lessons.line: A piece with no safe square, usually a bishop or a knight on the edge.

lessons.title: The in-between move
lessons.line: Before recapturing, a stronger move first.

lessons.title: Desperado
lessons.line: A piece that is lost anyway takes something with it.

lessons.title: Quiet moves
lessons.line: A combination where the key move is not a check or a capture.

lessons.title: Underpromotion
lessons.line: When a knight or a rook is better than a queen.

lessons.title: Perpetual check
lessons.line: Saving a lost game with checks that never end.
